article.articleHeadline: Alertă OMS: cea mai mare epidemie de Ebola din istoria Republicii Democrate Congo se extinde rapid
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO alert: the largest Ebola outbreak in the history of the Democratic Republic of the Congo is spreading rapidly.
article.articleSummary: WHO warns that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is expanding at an exceptional pace, now the largest ever recorded in the country. By 30 July, 3,605 cases and 1,587 deaths (case fatality ~44%) have been confirmed since the outbreak was declared on 15 May. The Bundibugyo variant has no licensed vaccine or approved treatment. In the most recent week with complete data, 567 new cases and 296 deaths were reported—the highest weekly toll since the start. The virus has spread from Ituri into North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo. Healthcare workers account for 151 infections, with 44 deaths. Insecurity, population movements, and cross-border mobility hinder intervention and raise regional spread risk. No approved Bundibugyo vaccine exists; Hilleman Laboratories (Singapore) is developing the most promising candidate, while Oxford University is testing an experimental vaccine, first dose administered. Authorities with WHO urge intensified response.

triage.headline_ja: WHO警報：コンゴ民主共和国史上最大規模のエボラ出血熱の流行が急速に拡大
triage.triage_reason: DRC史上最大のエボラ流行で、致死率約44%、複数州へ拡大、医療従事者感染多数、ワクチン未承認と、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: シンガポール（Hilleman Laboratories）と英国（オックスフォード大学）はワクチン開発拠点として言及されているのみで、感染発生国ではないため verified_locations から除外。

article.articleHeadline: Epidemie eboly nabývá na síle. Kongo hlásí tisíce případů za rekordně krátký čas!
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola epidemic is gaining strength. Congo reports thousands of cases in record time!
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak intensifies in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Ituri province) with Uganda. Since mid-May 2026, 3,533 confirmed cases—record-fast accumulation—and over 1,500 deaths (case fatality ~44.2%). Uganda has reportedly cleared the disease, but Congo’s spread remains uncontrolled, worsened by regional conflict and limited treatment; a rare Bundibugyo strain is driving the current outbreak. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus notes transmission outpacing response, with about two-thirds of deaths occurring outside healthcare facilities. Each confirmed urban case may have around 40 contacts; with roughly 3,400 cases, contact tracing could involve about 135,000 people. A Bundibugyo-targeted vaccine has reached clinical trial phase, with the first dose given last week, developed by Oxford University and the Serum Institute of India. The 2018–2020 Congo outbreak caused ~2,300 deaths out of ~3,500 cases; globally, Ebola has killed over 15,000 in 50 years, mostly in Africa.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ流行が勢いを増す。コンゴが記録的な短期間で数千人の症例を報告
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国での大規模エボラ流行（3,533例、致死率44.2%）で伝播が制御不能となっており、IHR基準の複数該当及び国際的関心・支援の必要性が高い。
triage.notes: ウガンダは既に終息と報告されているため、記事の主題はコンゴ（イトゥリ州）に限定。稀なブンディブギョ株による流行で、ワクチン臨床試験が開始された点も注視すべき。

article.articleHeadline: Bipartisan pair of senators urge Rubio to release aid to African women, children at risk of Ebola
article.articleSummary: Six Americans exposed are en route to safe withdrawal as the CDC coordinates after the WHO declared a health emergency linked to an Ebola outbreak in the DRC. As of July 29, the CDC reports 3,532 Ebola cases in DRC with 1,556 deaths; Uganda reports 20 cases, 2 deaths. The earliest case involved a health worker in Ituri who developed symptoms in late April and died; transmission may have begun as early as March. WHO alerted May 5 after four health workers died within four days; ten days later investigators confirmed Bundibugyo virus as the cause. Senators Murkowski and Shaheen urge State to release $608 million in international family-planning funds and $1.7 million in supplies stored in Geel, Belgium, to aid women and infants, warning they will be destroyed if unused. They seek humanitarian exception for UN Population Fund clinics in Uganda and DRC, arguing pregnancy and childbirth are catastrophic during Ebola.

triage.headline_ja: 超党派の上院議員2名、ルビオ長官にエボラのリスクにさらされるアフリカの女性・子供への支援解除を要請
triage.triage_reason: WHOがDRCのエボラ流行に関して緊急事態を宣言し、患者数3,532例・死亡1,556例、ウガンダへの拡大や米国人の曝露も確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大な公衆衛生イベントである。
triage.notes: ウガンダ、米国、ベルギーも記事に登場するが、対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。WHOによる緊急事態宣言や米上院議員の資金解除要請など、政治的関心も高いイベント。

article.articleHeadline: Kongo: Ebola-Ausbruch verschärft sich

article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in Congo, Central Africa, worsens as the number of infections reaches a new high. A test of a new Ebola vaccine is currently under way, while the risk of spread to neighboring countries increases. Despite weeks of efforts, the World Health Organization (WHO) has not managed to contain the outbreak in Central Africa. The report underscores ongoing transmission within the region and the potential for cross-border spread, heightening regional concern. Specific case and death counts are not provided in the text, but the description clearly indicates a deteriorating situation. The focus remains on Ebola in Central Africa with concern about neighboring nations as authorities monitor vaccine trial developments.

The article notes the Democratic Republic of Congo as the affected country, and Geneva as the briefing location. No specific case counts, symptoms, or laboratory confirmation are provided in the text. The warning underscores the severity of the ongoing outbreak observed by WHO officials.

article.articleHeadline: СЗО: Епидемијата на ебола во Конго се влошува и сега е најголема досега
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO: The Ebola outbreak in Congo is worsening and is now the largest ever.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo worsens, now the largest on record for the country, according to WHO. In the past week, 567 new infections and 296 deaths were reported, with laboratory-confirmed cases totaling 3,605 and 1,587 deaths; about 651 patients have recovered. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which there is no approved vaccine yet; a newly developed vaccine is undergoing testing. Previously the biggest outbreak (2018–2020) had 3,317 cases. The WHO notes improved surveillance and more tests contributing to higher counts, but containment requires increasing contact tracing to 95% (currently ~80%). The outbreak risks spread to neighboring countries. Health workers face dangerous conditions due to conflict with rebels, hundreds of thousands displaced, and deep public distrust hindering response efforts.

triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で過去最大規模のエボラ流行が発生し、致死率が高く、近隣国への拡大リスクや紛争による対応の困難さがあり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAが必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Bundibugyo strain outbreak worst ever in DR Congo, WHO says
article.articleSummary: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo strain, is the largest in the nation's history. Declared 15 May 2026, as of 30 July there were 3,605 confirmed cases and 1,587 deaths (case fatality ~44%). The World Health Organization notes the outbreak is intensifying with sustained transmission; the past week saw 567 new cases and 296 deaths—the highest weekly total to date. There is no approved vaccine or treatment for Bundibugyo, though vaccines are in development in the UK and Singapore. Transmission occurs via contact with bodily fluids. The outbreak centers in Ituri province in northeast DR Congo, which borders South Sudan and Uganda, and has spread to North and South Kivu, where much of the territory is controlled by the Rwanda-backed M23 group. Insecurity, displacement, and cross-border movement hinder response and risk further spread.

article.articleHeadline: Virus-Ausbruch verschärft sich - 296 Tote in einer Woche
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Virus Outbreak Worsens — 296 Dead in One Week.
article.articleSummary: DR Congo is contending with its largest Ebola outbreak to date, caused by the Bundibugyo variant. Over the past week, 567 new infections and 296 deaths were reported, bringing laboratory-confirmed cases to 3,605 and deaths to 1,587, with 651 recoveries. The World Health Organization warns the outbreak could spill into neighboring countries as control measures falter amid rebel conflict, mass displacement, and public mistrust. Only about 80% of contacts are observed for three weeks, far short of the 95% target, suggesting under-detection. Many patients never reach treatment centers, and funerals remain highly transmission-prone. No licensed vaccine exists for Bundibugyo; a newly developed vaccine is under trial. Investigators say the outbreak may have started in January, with Mongbwalu identified as an early epicenter.

article.articleHeadline: The Tiny Snails and Slugs That Can Turn Rat Lungworm into a Human Health Risk
article.articleSummary: Angiostrongylus cantonensis, rat lungworm, was described in 1933 in Guangzhou by H.T. Chen. Its life cycle requires rats as definitive hosts and snails or slugs as intermediate hosts; larvae migrate to the rat lungs, are shed in feces, infect gastropods, mature, then return to rats. Humans are incidental hosts via consumption of unwashed produce (notably lettuce) or paratenic hosts such as freshwater prawns, frogs, or fish. In humans, larvae enter the CNS and can cause eosinophilic meningitis; symptoms include neck pain, numbness, photophobia, headache, fever, and fatigue; severe cases can cause paralysis, coma, disability, or death. Since Guangzhou, A. cantonensis has spread across Southeast Asia, the Pacific Islands, Latin America, Australia, and warm parts of the U.S. (Hawaii, Florida, Gulf Coast) via ships, the pet trade (Achatina fulica, Pomacea), and climate change. Diagnosis relies on CSF eosinophils; prevention emphasizes washing produce and cooking potential hosts to 165°F.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the Congo raises global concern: it has spiraled out of control.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has intensified, described by WHO as the largest and most dangerous in the country’s history, with cross-border spread risk to neighboring states. In the past week, 567 new cases and 296 deaths were reported; total laboratory-confirmed cases now stand at 3,605 with 1,587 deaths and about 651 recoveries. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which there is no approved vaccine yet, though experimental vaccines are under evaluation. Challenges include insecurity from armed conflict, mass displacement, and deep public mistrust, hindering surveillance (only about 80% of contacts are monitored for three weeks; experts say 95% is needed). Safe burials and protective gear are being provided by NGOs to reduce transmission during funerals.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Health Organization: The Ebola outbreak in the Congo is out of control and the risk of its transmission is increasing.
article.articleSummary: World Health Organization reports Ebola outbreak in the Congo is out of control and transmission risk is rising. In the past week, 567 new infections and 296 deaths were recorded, the highest weekly rate since the start of the outbreak. The total laboratory-confirmed cases reach 3,605 with 1,587 deaths and 651 recoveries. The current surge surpasses the previous major wave (2018–2020), which had 3,317 confirmed infections. Despite improved surveillance and expanded laboratory testing, the rise reflects wider spread beyond prior detection. Contact tracing remains a major challenge, with around 80% of contacts of confirmed cases being monitored for three weeks; health experts say effective control requires at least 95% coverage. Ongoing outbreak and its expansion risk highlight urgent need for intensified public health measures.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue cases rise in dist; DMO calls for intensified mosquito control measures
article.articleSummary: Dengue cases are rising in T'puram district, prompting intensified Aedes mosquito control. District Medical Officer Dr. Bindu Mohan directed residents, institutions and local bodies to reinforce source-reduction efforts after intermittent rainfall created favorable breeding conditions. A district-wide cleaning drive will run Monday–Tuesday, with Dry Day observances: educational institutions on Fridays, commercial establishments and construction sites on Saturdays, and households and public spaces on Sundays. Emphasizing elimination of stagnant water where Aedes breed, households should inspect indoors and outdoors for breeding sites and avoid water accumulation in refrigerator drip trays, plant containers, discarded coconut shells, bottles, tyres and other outdoor items. Prevent stagnation on terraces, sunshades, roof gutters, plastic sheets and tarpaulins; keep water storage containers tightly covered. Use repellents, wear light clothing, install screens. Seek medical care for fever and body pain; don't send febrile children to school; stay hydrated and eat easily digestible foods.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO warns: Ebola is out of control in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: World Health Organization warns Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is escalating and outside containment, driven by the Bundibugyo strain spreading rapidly in the eastern region, particularly Ituri, where transmission may have started in January before official detection. The outbreak has no licensed vaccine or approved treatment; however, vaccines and therapies are under trial. Ongoing violence, displacement, and restricted access hinder contact tracing, isolation, and patient care. WHO has strengthened support with emergency response teams, enhanced surveillance, medical supplies, and additional treatment centers, and worked to coordinate with neighboring countries to curb cross-border transmission. In May, WHO categorized the outbreak as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. Experts describe it as the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history, amplifying concerns of spillover amid insecurity and funding gaps requiring urgent international assistance.

article.articleHeadline: WHO: Izbruh ebole v Kongu največji doslej
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO: Ebola outbreak in Congo largest to date.
article.articleSummary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is the largest to date, caused by the Bundibugyo variant for which no approved vaccine or therapy exists. A newly developed vaccine is currently undergoing trials. Experts believe the true number of infections is higher than reported, as many patients do not seek medical help and relatives often blame other illnesses for deaths. Burials pose heightened risk, since handling of the deceased can transmit Ebola to mourners. Humanitarian organizations are enabling safe, dignified burials with protective clothing and safety measures. The situation highlights gaps in treatment options and surveillance, even as vaccine candidates advance through development and testing.

article.articleHeadline: В ВОЗ предупредили о распространении лихорадки Эбола в ДРК с "исключительной скоростью"
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The WHO warned of the spread of Ebola virus disease in the DRC with exceptional speed.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is expanding at an exceptional speed, according to the World Health Organization. By the end of July 2026, about 3,605 confirmed cases have been reported, with more than half resulting in death, marking the largest outbreak on record in the DRC. In the most recent reporting week, 567 new cases were recorded, a record weekly total indicating rapid transmission. The strain circulating is Bundibugyo, for which there is no licensed vaccine. The outbreak began May 17 and prompted WHO to declare emergencies in DRC and Uganda. The recent pace contrasts with the 2018–2020 outbreak, which took over 10 months to reach a similar scale in fatalities. Affected regions include the DRC and neighboring Uganda, underscoring the urgent need for containment and vaccination development for this strain.

article.articleHeadline: Zoonoses de Várzea Grande faz alerta para alta de casos positivos e pede atenção da população aos sinais da doença
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Várzea Grande Zoonoses issues warning about rising positive cases and asks the public to pay attention to the signs of the disease.
article.articleSummary: Canine visceral leishmaniasis (LVC) is a rising concern in Várzea Grande, Brazil, an area long considered endemic, with increasing cases tied to expansion in neighborhoods like Jardim Maringá. LVC is a zoonosis caused by Leishmania sp., transmitted by sandflies (Lutzomyia longipalpis and related species); dogs are the main urban reservoir, elevating human risk. From January to June this year, the CCZ VG recorded nearly 500 tests on dogs suspected of LVC, signaling rising transmission. Classic canine symptoms include progressive weight loss with normal appetite, liver and spleen involvement, skin ulcers, and non-healing wounds, especially on the nose and ears. Euthanasia is only performed after confirmed diagnosis; Lacen provides final confirmation, with differential diagnoses including bacterial, fungal, autoimmune diseases, or mange. No mass vaccination; control emphasizes vector management and environmental measures, such as deltamethrin collars and yard cleaning. For testing, contact CCZ VG at Rua 42, Jardim Paiaguás I, (65) 98476-5719.

article.articleHeadline: إيبولا يخرج عن السيطرة في الكونغو - Lebanese Forces Official Website
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola Out of Control in Congo
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo remains out of control, per the WHO, with the current outbreak the largest in the country’s history, surpassing the 2018–2020 crisis (3,317 confirmed cases then). In the past week, 567 new infections and 296 deaths were reported, the highest weekly totals since the outbreak began. Lab-confirmed cases total 3,605 with 1,587 fatalities and 651 recoveries. Only about 80% of contacts are traced, well below the 95% target for effective containment. Ongoing security tensions and armed clashes hinder access to affected areas, displacing hundreds of thousands and increasing transmission risk. Community mistrust toward health authorities impedes surveillance and vaccination uptake. The outbreak poses a cross-border threat, underscoring the need for expanded response, vaccination, and public health measures to curb spread.

article.articleHeadline: إيبولا يستبد بالكونغو.. "الصحة العالمية" تحذّر: التفشي خارج السيطرة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola grips Congo... WHO warns: the outbreak is out of control.
article.articleSummary: As of 1 August 2026, the World Health Organization reports Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is still outside control and worsening, the largest outbreak the country has seen. Weekly figures show 567 new cases and 296 deaths—the highest weekly toll since the start of the outbreak. To date, 3,605 laboratory-confirmed cases have been reported, with 1,587 deaths and 651 recoveries. The ongoing outbreak has prompted WHO to call for a substantial expansion of response activities. The rise in numbers is attributed in part to improved surveillance and increased laboratory testing. This outbreak surpasses the previous major epidemic in 2018–2020, which recorded 3,317 confirmed cases. The article emphasizes the urgent need for intensified public health measures to regain control.

article.articleHeadline: Cea mai gravă epidemie de Ebola din istoria RD Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The most severe Ebola epidemic in the history of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: August 1, 2026 — The Democratic Republic of the Congo faces the most severe Ebola epidemic on record. As of July 30, 2026, official data show 3,605 confirmed cases and 1,587 deaths (44% mortality). The outbreak began in Mongbwalu, Ituri, and has spread in two months to five provinces: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo. The transmission rate remains unrelenting, with 567 new cases and 296 deaths reported in the latest week. The Bundibugyo variant drives the crisis, lacking a licensed vaccine or proven specific therapy. Healthcare workers account for 151 infections and 44 deaths. Cross-border spread remains a high risk; Uganda has declared its outbreak over, but vigilance is ongoing. Vaccination efforts include a WHO-promising candidate from Hilleman Laboratories (Singapore) and an Oxford University vaccine in trials, with a first dose given to a separate experimental vaccine candidate.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国史上最も深刻なエボラ流行

triage.triage_reason: エボラがDRC国内で史上最大規模に拡大し、5州に及ぶ持続的な人-人感染が確認されているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大なシグナル。

article.articleSummary: Outbreak: The World Health Organization reports that Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is out of control and expanding, with spillover risk to neighboring countries. As of 1 August 2026, 567 new cases and 296 deaths were recorded in the past week—the highest weekly total since the outbreak began. Cumulatively laboratory-confirmed cases total 3,605, with 1,587 deaths and 651 recoveries. This is the largest outbreak in the country to date, surpassing the 2018–2020 event (3,317 confirmed cases). article.articleHeadline: СЗО: Епидемијата на ебола во Конго се влошува

article.articleSummary: WHO reports the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is worsening and poses a higher risk of cross-border spread. The outbreak—the largest in the country to date—has intensified, with 567 new infections and 296 new deaths in the past week, bringing laboratory-confirmed cases to 3,605 and deaths to 1,587; about 651 patients have recovered. The previous major outbreak (2018–2020) recorded 3,317 confirmed cases. article.articleHeadline: DSÖ: Ebola salgını giderek şiddetleniyor
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO: The Ebola outbreak is intensifying.
article.articleSummary: As of July 30, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) — the country’s largest on record — is intensifying, driven by Bundibugyo virus. There are 3,605 laboratory-confirmed cases and 1,587 deaths (case fatality ~44%). Declared May 15, 2026, there is no approved vaccine or treatment for Bundibugyo; vaccines are in development in the United Kingdom and Singapore. Weekly counts peaked at 567 cases and 296 deaths. The epicenter is Ituri province in the northeast, near the borders with South Sudan and Uganda, with spread to North and South Kivu and areas controlled by the M23 group. Uganda reports 20 cases; France 1; two DRC cases were treated in Germany. Transmission occurs via direct contact with infected body fluids and contaminated objects; incubation is 2–21 days; early symptoms include fever, weakness, muscle pains, sore throat, followed by vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, rash, kidney/liver dysfunction, and potential bleeding.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en Ituri : 60 points d'entrée activés pour freiner efficacement la propagation de l'épidémie - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Ituri: 60 entry points activated to effectively curb the spread of the outbreak - ACP
article.articleSummary: On August 1, 2026, Ituri province in northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo activated 60 entry and control points to curb the Ebola virus outbreak, announced by Dr. Théophile Ponde, provincial coordinator of the National Border Health Program (PNHF). The reinforced checkpoints, deployed along major movement axes from Bunia, target epicenters Mongbwalu, Bunia, and Rwampara to monitor population flows and reduce transmission to areas not yet affected. The posts perform health screening of travelers, vehicles, and other transmission routes. The measure aims to strengthen the outbreak response by limiting cross-border and intra-provincial spread and complements ongoing containment efforts within affected zones.

article.articleHeadline: La Croix-Rouge sensibilise contre Ebola sur les principales artères de Kisangani - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Red Cross raises awareness about Ebola on Kisangani's main roads - ACP.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease awareness campaign by Red Cross volunteers in Kisangani, Tshopo Province, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, on August 1, 2026. About 210 trained volunteers are conducting outreach across six health zones—five in Kisangani and one in Bafwasende, 264 km away along RN4 toward Ituri, epicenter of the 17th Ebola outbreak. The efforts focus on symptoms, transmission, and prevention, delivered via songs and megaphone messages with slogans “Red Card to the deadly virus” and “Stop Ebola.” The operation accompanies the monthly health walk and aims to improve public understanding of Ebola signs and protection measures. Ituri Province is identified as the current epicenter of the outbreak, underscoring ongoing public-health education in affected regions.

article.articleHeadline: WHO: Izbruh ebole v DR Kongu največji doslej
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO: Ebola outbreak in the DRC the largest to date.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is the largest on record. In the past week, WHO reports 567 infections and 296 deaths, with total lab-confirmed cases over 3,600 and deaths over 1,580. The surge reflects enhanced testing, but signals broader spread. The Bundibugyo ebolavirus variant has no approved vaccine or treatment; a novel vaccine is in trials. Underreporting and unsafe burials likely understate the burden, though safe burial campaigns are underway. Transmission is by contact with bodily fluids. Africa CDC says $1.4B is needed; only about $213.9M has been raised for May–Aug, vs $242.4M planned. Armed groups in eastern DRC, reduced foreign aid, and US travel bans hinder response; WHO warns the true scale could be up to four times higher.

article.articleHeadline: OMS avertizează: Epidemia de Ebola din RD Congo se intensifică într-un ritm excepțional, cerând măsuri urgente * Newsweek România

article.articleHeadline: СЗО предупредува: Епидемијата на ебола во Конго се влошува, расте ризикот од ширење во регионот
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO warns: The Ebola outbreak in Congo is worsening, the risk of spread in the region is increasing.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo worsens with rising regional spread risk, per the WHO. This is the largest DRC outbreak to date, with 567 new infections and 296 deaths in the past week, bringing lab-confirmed cases to 3,605 and deaths to 1,587, plus 651 recoveries. The Bundibugyo variant drives transmission; no approved vaccine exists yet, though a new vaccine is in clinical trials. Some case rise reflects improved surveillance and testing, but contact tracing remains insufficient at about 80% of contacts followed, below the 95% target. Ongoing challenges include unstable security, clashes with armed groups, large displaced populations, and distrust of health authorities, all complicating containment and increasing the risk of spread to neighboring countries.

triage.headline_ja: WHO警告:コンゴのエボラ流行が悪化、地域への感染拡大リスクが増加
triage.triage_reason: DRCで過去最大規模のエボラ流行が悪化しており、致死率が高く、接触者追跡不足・治安不安・周辺国への拡大リスクがあるため、IHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: 承認済みワクチンが未だ存在せず、治験段階の新ワクチンがあることに留意。接触者追跡率が目標を下回っており、封じ込めの困難さと周辺国への拡大リスクが強調されている。

article.articleHeadline: 中國第三批伊波拉抗疫醫療專家組抵達剛果民主共和國　助防控疫情
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: China's third batch of Ebola outbreak medical experts arrives in the Democratic Republic of the Congo to assist in outbreak prevention and control.
article.articleSummary: Third batch of Ebola response medical experts from China arrived at Kinshasa airport in the Democratic Republic of the Congo to reinforce outbreak prevention and control. The delegation will bolster surveillance, patient care, and laboratory testing as the Ebola outbreak remains severe and under substantial pressure, according to the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ministry of Health. Led by Yang Xiaocheng, the team will build on the work of the first two batches, tailoring technical support to frontline needs and enhancing coordination with the health ministry and international partners to hasten control of the current outbreak. The mission underscores ongoing Chinese assistance to strengthen monitoring, diagnosis, and care capabilities, aiming to accelerate containment and eventual end of the Ebola crisis in the region.

triage.headline_ja: 中国の第3陣エボラ対応医療専門家チームがコンゴ民主共和国に到着、防疫を支援
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で進行中のエボラ出血熱の流行が深刻化しており、国際的な医療支援（中国からの専門家派遣）が継続的に必要とされているため、WPRO基準に複数該当しフルRRAでの評価が妥当と判断。
triage.notes: 記事は中国からの第3陣医療支援チーム派遣に関する内容であり、エボラ流行そのものはコンゴ民主共和国（キンシャサ）で発生・継続中。中国は支援提供国であり発生地域ではないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: منظمة الصحة العالمية: تفشي "إيبولا" في الكونغو الديمقراطية يخرج عن السيطرة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Health Organization: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is out of control.
article.articleSummary: As of 1 August 2026, the World Health Organization says the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is out of control, the largest on record. In the past week there were 567 new infections and 296 deaths, the highest weekly totals since the outbreak began. Total laboratory-confirmed cases: 3,605; deaths: 1,587; recoveries: 651. The prior largest outbreak (2018–2020) had 3,317 confirmed cases. A complex security situation—conflicts with rebels, mass displacement, and deep distrust of health authorities—hamstrings response. Only about 80% of contacts are being followed for three weeks, far short of the 95% target for control. Many patients do not reach treatment centers, and funeral rites remain high-risk. Aid organizations provide safe burials with protective gear. There is an elevated risk of cross-border transmission to neighboring countries.

triage.headline_ja: 世界保健機関:コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱の流行が制御不能に
triage.triage_reason: WHOが「制御不能」と表明した過去最大規模のエボラ流行であり、致死率・感染者数ともに急増し国境を越える伝播リスクも指摘されているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: WHOが史上最大規模と表明。週間感染者数・死亡者数ともに過去最高を記録し、接触者追跡率も目標未達。治安不安・住民の不信感が対応を阻害し、越境伝播リスクも指摘されている。

article.articleHeadline: DSÖ duyurdu: Ebola salgını kontrolden çıktı
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO announced: Ebola outbreak has gotten out of control.
article.articleSummary: WHO reports the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, centered in the eastern Ituri province, has reached uncontrollable and alarming levels. Since being declared on May 15, the outbreak has caused 1,556 deaths and 626 recoveries, with 807 people under isolation or closely monitored. The WHO declared an international public health emergency on May 17 due to the risk of further spread. Authorities note hundreds of suspected cases and dozens of deaths in Ituri. Laboratory confirmation identifies a Bundibugyo Ebola variant, for which there is no approved vaccine or specific treatment. Background context notes the virus was first identified in 1976 near the Ebola River in the DRC, and the 2014–2017 West Africa outbreak infected about 30,000 people and killed over 11,000. Emphasis remains on contact tracing, early detection, isolation, and increased international support to curb transmission.

triage.headline_ja: WHO発表:エボラ出血熱の流行が制御不能に陥る
triage.triage_reason: WHOが国際的な公衆衛生上の緊急事態を宣言し、致死率の高いエボラ出血熱(ブンディブギョ変異株)がコンゴ民主共和国で制御不能な水準に達しているため、IHR基準の複数該当及び国際的関心の高さからフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれるが、記事サマリーではDRC(イトゥリ州)のみが主題として述べられており、Angolaへの拡大に関する具体的言及はないため除外。致死率が非常に高く(1,556死亡/約3,000人規模)、ワクチン・治療法未承認のブンディブギョ変異株である点も重大なリスク要因。

article.articleHeadline: Campinas tem um caso de raiva em gato após 10 anos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Campinas has a case of rabies in a cat after 10 years.
article.articleSummary: Campinas, Brazil, reported the first feline rabies case since 2016. Devisa launched preventive actions including case investigation and active exposure tracing around the Cemitério da Saudade in the Swift neighborhood, where a young tabby with white belly was abandoned and died after illness. The animal tested positive for rabies at Pasteur Institute on July 29, 2026. A clinic worker who handled the cat was scratched but vaccinated and received post-exposure prophylaxis. UVZ is conducting house-to-house exposure checks. Exposed individuals should contact UVZ at (19) 2515-7044 for evaluation. The city’s last human rabies case was 1981; urban bats have produced 4 rabies cases so far this year, with 672 bats collected and 338 under investigation, and 18 bat rabies cases last year. Rabies is nearly always fatal; vaccination of dogs and cats annually, and immediate wound washing plus medical assessment after exposure.

triage.headline_ja: カンピナスで10年ぶりに猫の狂犬病症例
triage.triage_reason: 単発の猫の狂犬病症例であり、地域当局による適切な調査・曝露者へのワクチン接種等の対応が完了しており、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 地元保健当局(Devisa/UVZ)が曝露調査と予防対応を実施済み。都市部のコウモリ由来狂犬病は継続監視中だが、ヒト-ヒト感染のリスクはなく、地域限定的な事例。

article.articleHeadline: Experter varnar: Dödligt virus kan löpa amok på bara ett par veckor
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Experts warn: A deadly virus could run amok in as little as a couple of weeks.
article.articleSummary: Highly deadly avian influenza has spread to mammals worldwide, with Finland experiencing a severe outbreak on fur farms in summer 2023. In total, 27 farms housing tens of thousands of mink, foxes, and raccoon dogs were affected. Humans are at risk from contact with infected animals or their droppings; previous outbreaks in Asia showed case fatality rates approaching 50%, making avian influenza roughly 500 times deadlier than seasonal flu. As a drastic countermeasure, authorities culled and burned nearly 500,000 animals to stem the spread. Despite these efforts, the problem has worsened globally, fueling fears of human infection and potential human-to-human transmission. A groundbreaking study by Professor Gautam Menon of Ashoka University (India) claims to reveal how the virus will spread, with results described as a frightening surprise.

triage.headline_ja: 専門家警告：致死性ウイルスはわずか数週間で暴走しかねない
triage.triage_reason: 記事は2023年のフィンランドの毛皮農場における鳥インフルエンザ流行の総括と、インドの研究者による将来予測研究の紹介であり、対象国における現行の発生事例ではないため見送りとする。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はフィンランドの過去の毛皮農場アウトブレイク（2023年）に関する総括記事。インドは研究者（Ashoka University）の所属機関として言及されているのみで、実際の発生国ではないためverified_locationsから除外。フィンランドは対象国リストに含まれない。

article.articleHeadline: Eksperter advarer: Dødelig virus kan løbe løbsk på få uger
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Experts warn: A deadly virus could run amok in a few weeks.
article.articleSummary: Bird flu (avian influenza) has spread to mammals and researchers fear a human outbreak. In summer 2023, Finland faced a deadly wave on fur farms: 27 farms housing tens of thousands of mink, foxes, and raccoon dogs were hit. Nearly 500,000 animals were culled and burned to halt the spread. Humans are at risk through contact with infected animals or their remains, and past Asian outbreaks have shown case fatality rates near 50%, making avian influenza potentially around 500 times deadlier than seasonal flu. The threat is mounting globally. In a groundbreaking study, Professor Gautam Menon of Ashoka University (India) maps how the virus could spread, with findings described as alarmingly predictive. The article underscores ongoing concern about human infection and possible human-to-human transmission.

triage.headline_ja: 専門家警告：致死的ウイルスが数週間で制御不能になる可能性
triage.triage_reason: 記事は2023年のフィンランドの毛皮農場における鳥インフルエンザ流行の回顧とインドの研究者による理論的な感染拡大モデル研究を紹介するものであり、対象国における実際の発生事象ではないため見送りとする。
triage.notes: 記事は主にフィンランドでの過去（2023年）の鳥インフルエンザ流行と、インド在住研究者による将来的な感染拡大シミュレーション研究を扱っており、対象国（India含む）での実際の発生事例を報告するものではない。インドは研究者の所属機関として言及されているのみで、発生地ではないため verified_locations に含めない。

article.articleHeadline: 刚果（金）埃博拉疫情确诊病例超3500例
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo exceeds 3,500 confirmed cases.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached 3,532 confirmed cases and 1,556 deaths as of July 31, 2026, a case fatality rate of about 44.1%, making it the second-largest outbreak to date. Some 807 patients remain in isolation or under treatment, with 626 recovered. The outbreak is centered in Ituri province and has spread to North Kivu, South Kivu, Upper Uele, and Chopo. It is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus; there is currently no approved vaccine or specific treatment. The United Nations calls the spread rapid, and Africa CDC notes a high fatality rate, with deaths in the first three months five times higher than during similar previous outbreaks. These figures reflect ongoing, severe transmission and a challenging public health response.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱、確認症例3,500例超
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約44%・症例数3,500超の大規模流行で複数州に拡大しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: ワクチン未承認・特効薬なしで致死率が過去の類似流行の5倍とされ、国連やAfrica CDCも急速な拡大を指摘。複数州（イトゥリ、北キブ、南キブ、オートウエレ、チョポ）にまたがる大規模流行。

article.articleHeadline: الصحة العالمية: تفشي إيبولا في الكونغو يخرج عن السيطرة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Health Organization: Ebola outbreak in the Congo spirals out of control.
article.articleSummary: World Health Organization reports Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains out of control as of 1 August 2026, with the situation worsening and cross-border transmission risk to neighboring countries. The current outbreak is the largest in DRC history, surpassing the 2018–2020 outbreak that had 3,317 confirmed cases. In the past week, 567 new cases and 296 deaths were recorded—the highest weekly totals since the outbreak began. Laboratory-confirmed cases total 3,605, with 1,587 deaths and 651 recoveries. WHO urged a substantial expansion of response activities to curb transmission. The outbreak’s persistently rising case load underscores the need for intensified public health measures to prevent further spread to adjacent nations.

triage.headline_ja: 世界保健機関：コンゴのエボラ出血熱の流行が制御不能に
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最大規模のエボラ流行が制御不能となっており、致死率も高く、周辺国への越境感染リスクが指摘されているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: WHOが対応の大幅拡大を要請しており、史上最大規模の流行かつ致死率約44%（1587/3605）と極めて深刻。フルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: 어디서 걸렸는지도 몰라" 벌써 1500명 사망...치료제 없는 에볼라, 급격 확산
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: "We don't even know where they got infected" Already 1,500 dead... Ebola with no cure, spreading rapidly.
article.articleSummary: An Ebola outbreak centered in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is accelerating, rapidly approaching the scale of the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic. As of July 29, 2026, confirmed cases reached 3,532 (up 90 in 1 day), with 1,556 deaths (case fatality rate 44.1%). About 807 patients are in isolation or hospital care, and 626 have recovered. The circulating strain is Bundibugyo Ebola virus, for which no approved vaccine or therapy exists and CFR is typically 30–50%. This outbreak exceeds the 2018–2020 DRC outbreak in case numbers (3,481) and is the second-largest globally after West Africa. Ituri Province hosts early-stage treatment trials; however, global surveillance suggests actual infections may be 2–4 times higher. Roughly 80% of new cases have unknown infection sources. Access is impeded by armed groups in eastern DRC and reduced international aid, hampering containment and contact tracing.

triage.headline_ja: 「どこで感染したのかも分からない」すでに1500人死亡…治療薬のないエボラ、急速に拡大
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ(ブンディブギョ株)アウトブレイクが西アフリカ流行に次ぐ規模に急拡大し、致死率44%、感染経路不明例が8割に達するなど公衆衛生上深刻かつ国際的拡大リスクが高いため、フルRRAへの移行が必要。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれるが、記事サマリーではDRC(特にIturi州)が主題であり、Angolaに関する言及はないため除外した。武装勢力の活動や国際支援の減少により封じ込めが困難な状況であり、続報の注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Malaria: Preventable killer we must no longer ignore, By Nosimot Soneye
article.articleSummary: Malaria remains a leading preventable killer in Africa. Global: 282 million cases and 610,000 deaths in 2024; Africa accounts for 94% of cases and 95% of deaths, with 75% of deaths in children under five. Nigeria ranks among the countries bearing over half the global burden, alongside the DRC, Ethiopia, Mozambique and Uganda. In Ogun State, Nigeria, Governor Dapo Abiodun’s administration has sustained malaria-reduction and healthcare-access efforts. Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes, mainly biting at dusk and dawn; transmission from mother to unborn child is possible. Symptoms include fever, chills, headache, weakness and sweating; diagnosis should be confirmed via blood microscopy or rapid diagnostic tests before treatment. Artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT) is recommended after confirmation. WHO warns of drug resistance, climate change, and funding gaps; World Malaria Day 2026 theme: Driven to End Malaria—Now We Can; Now We Must.

triage.headline_ja: マラリア:もはや無視できない予防可能な殺し屋 — ノシモット・ソネイエ
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はマラリアの世界的・アフリカの疾病負荷に関する啓発・論説記事であり、特定の異常な発生や急増を報告するものではないため、シグナルとしての該当性は低い。
triage.notes: 記事はマラリアに関する世界啓発デー(World Malaria Day)関連の一般的な論説であり、DRC等は既知の流行国として言及されているのみで、新規の発生・急増報告ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Surto de Ebola no Congo se torna o maior já registrado no país e continua a crescer
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in Congo becomes the largest ever recorded in the country and continues to grow.
article.articleSummary: As of July 30, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has grown to 3,605 cases and 1,587 deaths, up 13% from the previous week, per the World Health Organization. Caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, the outbreak is the largest ever recorded in the DRC and has spread to five provinces. The crude case fatality rate is about 44%. In the most recent full week, 567 new confirmed cases and 296 deaths were reported, the highest weekly totals since the start of the outbreak, underscoring rapid transmission despite a broad response by national authorities and international partners, alongside intensified surveillance and case finding.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行、同国史上最大規模となり拡大が続く
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最大規模のエボラ流行が発生し、致死率約44%、5州へ拡大、週間新規感染者・死者数が過去最多を記録しており、IHR基準の複数項目に該当する。
triage.notes: WHOの報告に基づく大規模アウトブレイク。既存のRRA/フォローアップ対象である可能性が高く、続報の追跡が必要。

article.articleHeadline: الصحة العالمية تحذر من إيبولا في الكونغو.. ماذا يحدث؟
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Health Organization warns of Ebola in Congo... What is happening?
article.articleSummary: As of 1 August 2026, the World Health Organization warns that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is spiraling out of control, with new infections continuing in multiple areas and growing concerns about broader transmission. Response teams face major obstacles, including restricted access to affected zones, shortages of medical and logistical resources, and security challenges hindering operations. WHO urges intensified international support—funding, equipment, and specialized personnel—to strengthen early case detection, contact tracing, vaccination campaigns, and health‑facility readiness. Ebola spreads through direct contact with blood or body fluids and contaminated surfaces, underscoring the need for rapid, coordinated action to curb transmission. While containment remains possible, it requires urgent, wide‑scale international cooperation to prevent spread to new areas and reduce health and humanitarian impacts, given ongoing cases across several African countries.

triage.headline_ja: 世界保健機関、コンゴでのエボラ出血熱を警告…何が起きているのか？
triage.triage_reason: WHOがコンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ流行が制御不能になりつつあると警告しており、複数地域での新規感染、国際的拡大懸念、渡航・貿易への影響可能性からIHR基準複数該当が想定される。
triage.notes: 記事はWHOの警告に基づく速報的内容であり、具体的な症例数や地域名の詳細は本文に記載がないため、続報での確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Africa in July: Uganda's Ebola 'victory', strained S'Africa continental ties, Nigeria-Morocco gas pipeline
article.articleSummary: Uganda discharged the last Ebola patient in July, signaling a potential end to the outbreak and raising prospects of an Ebola-free status. In South Africa, xenophobic violence intensified, straining continental ties as Nigeria reported further fatalities: a Nigerian citizen, Ibeh Simon, and another were killed during a Cape Town SAPS operation, bringing current-wave Nigerian deaths to five and total killings since 2022 to about 98 (mob violence, hate crimes, and extrajudicial killings). A South African delegation to Abuja, led by Ronald Lamola, saw a downgraded meeting with President Tinubu. Ghana lodged a protest over a planned Ramaphosa visit, urging deferral until xenophobia issues are resolved, though officials stated the relationship remains intact. Ghana also moved to extend the presidential term from four to five years, extending Parliament similarly, lowering the presidential candidate age to 35, and shifting elections to the first week of November with a January inauguration timeline.

triage.headline_ja: 7月のアフリカ情勢：ウガンダのエボラ「勝利」、南ア・アフリカ大陸関係の緊張、ナイジェリア・モロッコ間ガスパイプライン
triage.triage_reason: ウガンダでのエボラ流行は最後の患者退院により終息に向かっているとの報道であり、新規の公衆衛生上の脅威ではない。また対象国リストにウガンダは含まれず、記事内のガーナへの言及もエボラとは無関係の政治的話題である。
triage.notes: この記事は月次のアフリカ情勢まとめであり、エボラに関しては流行終息（最後の患者退院）を報じる内容。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれておらず、ガーナへの言及はエボラとは無関係の政治的トピック（大統領任期延長など）のため、verified_locationsは空とした。

article.articleHeadline: População de 6 meses a 59 anos deve se vacinar contra o sarampo em três cidades da Grande São Paulo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Population aged 6 months to 59 years should be vaccinated against measles in three cities in the Greater São Paulo area.
article.articleSummary: Measles vaccination drive targets residents aged 6 months to 59 years in São Paulo, Guarulhos, and São Bernardo do Campo after 15 confirmed measles cases in 2026. Starting Monday, August 3, people in these cities should seek the triple viral vaccine (MMR), which protects against measles, mumps, and rubella, even if previously vaccinated. The latest case occurred in Guarulhos in a child who was not vaccinated; of the 15 cases in the state this year, 12 were in the capital, two in São Bernardo do Campo, and one in Guarulhos. Travelers returning from World Cup host countries should monitor for fever, cough, rash, runny nose, conjunctivitis, and malaise. In other São Paulo municipalities, multivaccination activities will update vaccination records for children and adolescents under 15; bring the vaccination card and ID. Dose zero applies for 6–11 months and does not replace scheduled doses at 12 and 15 months. Statewide 2026 coverage: ~77.5% first dose, ~65.5% second dose; target is 95% for each dose.

triage.headline_ja: サンパウロ大都市圏の3都市で生後6ヶ月〜59歳の住民が麻疹ワクチン接種を受けるべき
triage.triage_reason: ブラジル・サンパウロ州で麻疹症例が15件確認され、ワクチンカバレッジが目標(95%)を大きく下回る（1回目77.5%、2回目65.5%）ため流行しやすい状況にあり、州政府が緊急ワクチン接種キャンペーンを実施している点で社会的・行政的関心が認められる。
triage.notes: サンパウロ州の麻疹排除国としての地位再燃リスクと低ワクチン接種率が懸念材料。ワールドカップ開催国からの帰国者への注意喚起も含まれており、国際的な人の移動との関連性も示唆される。症例数自体は少なく重症例・死亡の報告はないため、続報を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Dünya Sağlık Örgütü duyurdu! Salgın kontrolden çıkıyor: Nadir varyant tespit edildi
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO announced! The outbreak is getting out of control: A rare variant has been detected.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, centered in Ituri province ( eastern DRC ), has intensified. The outbreak, officially declared on 15 May, is caused by the Bundibugyo Ebola virus variant, a rare strain with no approved vaccine or specific treatment. The World Health Organization declared an international public health emergency on 17 May and urging intensified contact tracing, early diagnosis, isolation, and increased international support. By 1 August 2026, the toll reached 1,556 deaths and 626 recoveries, with 807 individuals in isolation or under surveillance. Common symptoms include high fever and hemorrhagic fever. The infection source was not disclosed in the report; no mention of imported or exported cases is provided. The situation follows hundreds of suspected cases and dozens of deaths reported earlier in Ituri.

triage.headline_ja: 世界保健機関が発表!流行が制御不能に:希少な変異株が検出された
triage.triage_reason: WHOが国際的な公衆衛生上の緊急事態を宣言し、エボラ出血熱(ブンディブギョ株)による多数の死者・症例が発生しているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: WHOが国際的公衆衛生上の緊急事態(PHEIC)を宣言済み。ワクチン・特効薬未承認の希少変異株(ブンディブギョ株)による大規模流行で、致死率・感染規模ともに深刻。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC : l'OMS alerte sur la plus grave épidémie jamais enregistrée dans le pays
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC: WHO warns of the most severe outbreak ever recorded in the country.
article.articleSummary: 3,605 laboratory-confirmed Ebola virus disease cases and 1,587 deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo as of 30 July 2026 (case fatality 44%), with at least 651 recoveries. The Bundibugyo strain outbreak originated in Mongbwalu, Ituri, and over two months spread to five provinces—Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu, Haut-Uélé, and Tshopo—affecting 49 health zones. WHO notes accelerated transmission: Week 30 recorded 567 new confirmed cases and 296 deaths; since 17 July, 1,481 new cases and 759 deaths. Ituri accounts for about 88% of cases and >82% of deaths. Contacts under follow-up total 17,863; 151 health workers have been infected, 44 have died. The response is challenged by armed conflict, displacement, and attacks on health facilities, necessitating a massive scale-up. Uganda ended its outbreak on 28 July after 42 days with no local transmission, but reintroduction risk remains. There is no licensed vaccine or specific treatment for Bundibugyo Ebola; control relies on rapid case detection, isolation, contact tracing, safe burials, and community adherence.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：コンゴ民主共和国、同国史上最も深刻な流行にWHOが警鐘
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で3,600例超・致死率44%の大規模エボラ流行が5州49保健地域に拡大し、WHOが同国史上最悪と警告。武力紛争により対応が困難で国際的拡大リスクも高い。
triage.notes: ウガンダは42日間の無伝播期間を経て流行終息を宣言済み（再導入リスクは残存）だが対象国リストに含まれないため除外。感染力の強いBundibugyo株で承認済みワクチン・治療薬がなく、医療従事者151名感染・44名死亡と医療体制への深刻な影響あり。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en Ituri : les points de contrôle comme espaces de filtrage contre la propagation (Programme national d'hygiène aux frontières) - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Ituri: checkpoints as screening spaces to curb the spread (National Border Hygiene Program) - ACP
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak response in Ituri Province, northeast Democratic Republic of the Congo (Bunia), deploys temporary checkpoint posts as sanitary screening spaces along major movement axes to detect suspected Ebola cases early and curb spread. Dr Théophile Ponde, head of the Entry Points and Checkpoints pillar of the National Border Hygiene Program (PNHF), said these screening posts operate during a health emergency to reinforce surveillance of population movements. They perform health assessments of travelers and rapidly direct individuals with signs compatible with Ebola to care teams. The posts supplement permanent checks at official entry points—borders, ports, and airports—to reduce transmission between zones within the province. The public is urged to cooperate with field teams to protect communities and strengthen the response, as of August 1, 2026.

triage.headline_ja: イツリ州のエボラ出血熱:検問所を感染拡大防止のためのスクリーニング拠点として活用（国境衛生プログラム）
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱はIHR上重大な公衆衛生イベントであり、DRCイツリ州での継続的なアウトブレイク対応（検問所設置等）が報告されており、国際的拡大リスクも否定できないためフルRRAへ進める。
triage.notes: 記事は既存のエボラアウトブレイク対応（検問所設置による人流管理）についての続報であり、新規発生の詳細（症例数・死亡者数）は記載されていないため、感染規模や重症度の詳細情報はRRAで確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola : la frontière RDC-Ouganda sous surveillance renforcée en Ituri - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: the DRC–Uganda border under heightened surveillance in Ituri - ACP
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak prompts heightened cross-border surveillance along the DR Congo–Uganda frontier in Ituri (Nord-East DR Congo) as part of the response. In Bunia, on 1 August 2026, Dr Théophile Ponde, provincial coordinator of the National Border Hygiene Program (PNHF) and head of the Entry Points and Control Points pillar, said the DRC has not closed its borders. The approach emphasizes reinforced surveillance, early detection, and rapid bilateral response under International Health Regulations to avoid unnecessary disruptions to trade. Cross-border mechanisms have been strengthened with Uganda through transboundary meetings to assess surveillance and response capacities in border zones. Entry points have enhanced health checks to screen travelers, identify suspected cases, and refer them to appropriate facilities. Regional support includes boosting Ugandan health capacities to manage any cases, aiming to limit Ebola export or import while maintaining effective cross-border surveillance.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ:イトゥリ州のコンゴ民主共和国・ウガンダ国境で監視強化 - ACP
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱のアウトブレイクに伴い、DRC-ウガンダ国境で越境監視体制が強化されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCのイトゥリ州における国境監視強化が主題。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC : " C'est le pire endroit au monde pour affronter une telle épidémie ", explique la responsable de la cellule d'urgence

article.articleSummary: Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is intensifying at an 'exceptional' pace as of August 1, 2026, per the World Health Organization. It is described as the largest Ebola outbreak ever reported in the DRC, with sustained transmission and a continuous rise in reported cases and deaths. Livia Tampellini, MSF's medical head of the emergency unit, who spent much of July on the ground, explains the worsening on-the-ground situation. The available excerpt does not provide granular details such as case counts, symptoms, laboratory confirmation, or infection sources.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱DRC流行：「このような流行に立ち向かうには世界最悪の場所」と緊急対応部門責任者が説明
triage.triage_reason: DRCにおけるエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）流行がWHOにより「過去最大規模」「例外的な速度で拡大」と評されており、公衆衛生上深刻かつ国際的拡大リスクがあるためフルRRAへ進めるべき。

article.articleHeadline: الصحة العالمية: إيبولا خارج السيطرة في الكونغو الديمقراطية - هبة بريس
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Health Organization: Ebola Out of Control in the Democratic Republic of the Congo - Hiba Press
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains out of control, warned by the World Health Organization. Over the past week, 567 new infections and 296 deaths were recorded, the highest weekly toll since the crisis began. Cumulative confirmed cases reach 3,605, with 1,587 deaths and 651 recoveries. Containment relies on expanding response activities, as WHO teams can currently trace only about 80% of contacts; tracing at least 95% is needed to curb transmission. While enhanced surveillance and testing have identified more cases, the rise also signals a widening spread. Ongoing conflict, access barriers, and large displaced populations hinder vaccination campaigns and contact tracing, undermining trust in health authorities and elevating the risk of further spread within the DRC and to neighboring countries.

triage.headline_ja: 世界保健機関(WHO):コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱が制御不能に - ヒバプレス

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak in Congo remains out of control, WHO warns
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo remains out of control and expanding, with increasing risk of cross-border transmission. It is the largest outbreak in the DRC’s history, surpassing the 2018–2020 wave of 3,317 cases. Last week saw 567 new cases and 296 deaths, bringing laboratory-confirmed cases to 3,605 and deaths to 1,587, with 651 recoveries. Despite better case detection and expanded laboratory testing, the rise in numbers reflects wider geographic spread rather than detection alone. Contact tracing remains a major challenge, with only about 80% of contacts monitored for three weeks; experts say coverage must reach at least 95% to curb transmission. The World Health Organization calls for a significant scale-up of the health response to limit spread and reduce cross-border risk.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行、依然として制御不能とWHOが警告
triage.triage_reason: DRC史上最大規模のエボラ流行が拡大を続け、国境を越えた感染リスクが増大しており、WHOが対応強化を呼びかけている。IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大な公衆衛生事案。
triage.notes: 致死率が高く（1,587/3,605、約44%）、接触者追跡のカバー率も目標に届いていない。国境を越えた拡大リスクが明示されており、フルRRAへの移行が妥当。

article.articleHeadline: Áp xe mang tai, bất ngờ phát hiện nhiễm vi khuẩn 'ăn thịt người'
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Parotid abscess, unexpectedly discovered infection with flesh-eating bacteria.
article.articleSummary: 60-year-old man in Phú Thọ, Vietnam, presented with swelling and pain near the right ear, initially diagnosed on 1 August as cellulitis with an abscess of the parotid gland. An incision and drainage was performed; pus sent for culture identified Burkholderia pseudomallei, the agent of Whitmore/Melioidosis. The infection is soil- and waterborne and can cause septicemia and multi-organ damage; the exposure timing remains unclear for this patient. He received antibiotics; fever resolved and the parotid abscess decreased. Melioidosis mortality can be high: septicemia-related deaths around 40–50% in Thailand/Singapore, and up to 75% with pneumonia. There is currently no vaccine. Protective measures include PPE for outdoor work, hand hygiene, and avoiding undercooked meat. Clinicians should consider melioidosis in persistent swelling with fever or pus and seek early hospital evaluation. Published 2 August 2026.

triage.headline_ja: 耳下腺膿瘍、思いがけず「人食いバクテリア」感染が判明
triage.triage_reason: 単発の個別症例報告であり、地域的な集団発生やヒト-ヒト感染の兆候はなく、公衆衛生上の異常性・国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 類鼻疽（メリオイドーシス）は土壌・水系感染症であり、ヒト-ヒト感染は起こらない。単発症例のため経過観察の必要性も低い。タイ・シンガポールの致死率は一般的背景情報として記載されているのみで、当該国での発生ではない。

triage.headline_ja: 世界保健機関(WHO):コンゴ民主共和国における今回のエボラ出血熱流行は同国史上最大規模

article.articleHeadline: WHO upozorava da se epidemija ebole u Kongu pogoršava
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO warns that the Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is worsening.
article.articleSummary: As of 1 August 2026, the World Health Organization warns that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is worsening. In the past week, 567 new infections and 296 deaths were recorded, the highest weekly totals to date. Overall, lab-confirmed cases reach 3,605 with 1,587 fatalities; 651 patients have recovered. The current epidemic is caused by the Bundibugyo virus variant, for which there is no approved vaccine, and clinical trials are ongoing. Health workers face severe security challenges, including clashes with armed groups, mass displacement of hundreds of thousands, and deep public mistrust. triage.headline_ja: WHO、コンゴのエボラ流行が悪化していると警告
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最悪規模のエボラ流行が継続・悪化しており、致死率が高く、承認済みワクチンがなく、越境拡大リスクをWHOが警告しているためIHR基準を複数満たす。

article.articleHeadline: पूर्वी सिंहभूम में मलेरिया से दहशत: बोड़ाम में बच्ची की मौत के बाद दो भाई MGM में भर्ती, 1 दिन में मिले 64 नए मरीज - east singhbhum malaria outbreak child dies 64 new cases
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Malaria scare in East Singhbhum: after the death of a girl in Bodam, two brothers admitted to MGM Medical College and Hospital, 64 new cases reported in one day.
article.articleSummary: Malaria outbreak intensifies in East Singhbhum, India. In Bodam block’s Dhobani village, a 5-year-old girl died two days earlier; two other siblings are now hospitalized at MGM Medical College and Hospital. A 3-year-old boy, Gau Singh, is in ICU and his 12-year-old brother Sundar Singh remains in the pediatric ward; both have confirmed malaria. MGM’s pediatric ward currently treats five children with malaria from various areas. During Saturday’s mass screening across blocks, 6,666 people were tested and 64 were positive: 50 cerebral malaria (Plasmodium falciparum), 13 vivax malaria (Plasmodium vivax), and 1 mixed infection. Health authorities have stepped up surveillance, rapid testing, and drug distribution in affected areas. The public is urged to seek examination promptly for high fever, shivering, or extreme weakness.

triage.headline_ja: 東部シングブーム県でマラリア恐慌:ボーダムで少女死亡後、兄弟2人がMGM病院に入院、1日で新規64例確認
triage.triage_reason: インド・ジャールカンド州でマラリアによる死亡例と多数の新規陽性例(脳性マラリア含む)が報告されているが、地域限定の風土病アウトブレイクであり国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低い。続報を注視する。
triage.notes: マラリアはインド東部で風土病的に発生しており、今回の報告は地域内の季節性アウトブレイクの一部と考えられる。死亡例や脳性マラリアの重症例があるため地域保健当局の対応状況を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Au Congo, l'épidémie d'Ebola s'intensifie à un rythme "exceptionnel", l'OMS constate "une augmentation continue du nombre de cas signalés et de décès".
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In the Congo, the Ebola outbreak is intensifying at an 'exceptional' pace, the WHO notes 'a continued increase in the number of reported cases and deaths'.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is intensifying at an exceptional pace due to the Bundibugyo variant, for which no treatment exists. triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ流行が『例外的な』速さで激化、WHOは報告症例数と死者数の継続的増加を確認

article.articleHeadline: Kasus DBD Masih Tinggi, Edukasi 3M Digencarkan ke Sekolah Dasar
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue Fever Cases Remain High; 3M Education Intensified in Elementary Schools
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever cases in Indonesia remained high, with 161,752 cases and 673 deaths in 2025, and 39,672 cases with 105 deaths by mid-2026; children aged 5–14 accounted for about 41% of dengue deaths. In response, the Enesis Group, in collaboration with the Ministry of Health, Jakarta Health Office, and Jakarta Education Office, launched ASEAN Dengue Day 2026 under CSR to support Indonesia Zero Dengue Death by 2030. The program features roadshows at several elementary schools (SDN 03 and SDN 05 Tanah Tinggi, SDN 20 Utan Kayu Selatan, SDN 02 Mampang Prapatan) to promote the 3M+ actions: drain standing water, cover water containers, repurpose waste likely to hold rainwater, and protect against mosquito bites. Officials stress multi-sector involvement and sustained habits, aiming to institutionalize dengue prevention in schools, homes, and communities and inspire similar initiatives across ASEAN.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱症例依然高水準、小学校での3M教育活動を強化
triage.triage_reason: デング熱はインドネシアで毎年発生する風土病であり、本記事は既存の予防啓発活動の紹介が中心だが、死亡者数（特に小児）が高いことから重症度基準に該当し経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: 記事は2025年及び2026年上半期の統計を示し、政府・保健省主導の予防教育キャンペーン（3M+運動）に焦点を当てている。新規の異常な発生というより既存の風土病対策の継続報道。

article.articleHeadline: الصحة العالمية: إيبولا يخرج عن السيطرة في الكونغو الديمقراطية

article.articleHeadline: DSÖ alarm verdi! Ebola salgını kontrolden çıktı
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO Issues Alarm! Ebola Outbreak Out of Control.
article.articleSummary: As of 1 August 2026, Ebola outbreaks persist in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), with 3,532 confirmed cases and 1,556 deaths; 626 recovered and 807 still in isolation. Authorities have intensified border health checks and contact tracing to prevent cross-border spread, while emphasis remains on early detection, isolation, and tracing contacts.

triage.headline_ja: WHOが警告！エボラ流行が制御不能に
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）が3,532例・1,556死亡と大規模化し、WHOが国際的公衆衛生上の緊急事態を宣言、承認済みワクチン・治療薬が無いため国際的拡大リスクと渡航制限リスクが高い。
triage.notes: WHOによる国際的公衆衛生上の緊急事態(PHEIC)宣言済み。承認されたワクチン・治療薬がないブンディブギョ株であり、致死率が高く、越境拡大防止のための国境検疫強化が実施されている点にも注意。

article.articleHeadline: Mato Grosso do Sul soma mais de 10 mil casos de hepatites virais
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mato Grosso do Sul records more than 10,000 cases of viral hepatitis.
article.articleSummary: Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, registered 10,199 viral hepatitis cases and 986 deaths from 2000–2024, highlighting that early diagnosis boosts cure chances as infections can be silent and progress to cirrhosis, liver cancer, or transplant. Nationally, Brazil reported over 826,000 hepatitis cases (2000–2024): hepatitis C 342,328 (41.5%), hepatitis B 302,351 (36.6%), hepatitis A 174,977 (21.2%), with hepatitis D and E together <1%. In MS, hepatitis A accounted for the highest notifications during 2000–2024. To improve detection, the Health Ministry distributed rapid tests, with 60,000 hepatitis C tests delivered to MS by May 2026. Transmission differs by type: HAV via contaminated water/food; HBV/HDV via blood, unprotected sex, and mother-to-child; HCV via blood contact and non-sterile procedures. The Global Hepatitis Report 2026 cites ~1.3 million deaths in 2024 from HBV/HCV worldwide, challenging elimination by 2030.

triage.headline_ja: マット・グロッソ・ド・スル州、ウイルス性肝炎の症例が1万件を超える
triage.triage_reason: 2000〜2024年の長期累積統計に基づく啓発的な内容であり、急性の公衆衛生上の異常事態や新規アウトブレイクを示すものではない。
triage.notes: 記事は2000〜2024年の統計データに基づく報告であり、急性の感染症アウトブレイクを示すものではない。検査キット配布など既存の対策強化に関する内容。

article.articleHeadline: ВОЗ сделала неутешительные выводы о масштабах эпидемии Эболы
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO has drawn sobering conclusions about the scale of the Ebola epidemic.
article.articleSummary: As of July 30, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is the largest in the country’s history, per the World Health Organization. There are 3,605 confirmed cases and 1,587 deaths, a case fatality rate of 44%. In the most recent complete reporting week, 567 new cases and 296 deaths were recorded, signaling exceptionally rapid spread. The 17th Ebola outbreak began on May 15 and has affected three provinces in the DRC, with spillover into neighboring Uganda. WHO has previously warned that the true number of infections could be roughly twice the officially confirmed 2,500 cases, underscoring ongoing escalation and cross-border transmission concerns.

triage.headline_ja: WHOがエボラ流行の規模について厳しい見解を示す
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で史上最大規模のエボラ流行が発生し、致死率44%、急速な拡大とウガンダへの越境伝播が確認されているため、IHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: ウガンダへの越境伝播が報告されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。DRCの流行が史上最大規模であり、真の感染者数は報告数の約2倍に達する可能性がWHOにより指摘されている。

article.articleHeadline: SMS awaits culture reports to find cataract infection source
article.articleSummary: Five patients with severe post-cataract infections at Kuchaman City's government's hospital were sampled for culture to identify the organism and trace the source. The surgeries occurred on July 28; all five were moved to Jaipur's SMS Hospital and underwent vitrectomy on July 30, with antibiotics started immediately. Culture results are awaited to confirm the causative organism and determine if the current antibiotic regimen should be changed. Findings may help investigators assess whether infections stemmed from surgical instruments, consumables, medicines, sterilisation lapses, or another common exposure at the facility. Outcomes depend on infection severity at treatment start, retinal involvement, and response to intensive medical and surgical management over the next days, with visual prognosis closely monitored.

triage.headline_ja: SMS病院、白内障感染症の感染源特定のため培養検査結果を待つ
triage.triage_reason: 同一病院での白内障術後感染クラスター（5例）だが、院内感染管理の問題であり感染症としての国際的拡大リスクは低い。原因菌・感染源が未確定のため続報を注視。
triage.notes: 白内障手術後の眼内炎クラスターであり、感染症アウトブレイクというより医療施設内の感染管理事案。培養結果と原因究明の続報を待つ必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: DSÖ'den Korkutan Uyarı: Ölümcül Virüs Kontrolden Çıkıyor
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Alarming Warning from the WHO: The Deadly Virus Is Getting Out of Control.
article.articleSummary: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has been declared in eastern Ituri Province, officially announced on May 15. As of August 1, 2026, the Health Ministry reports 1,556 deaths and 626 recoveries, with 807 people in isolation; hundreds of suspected cases and dozens of deaths have occurred in Ituri. The outbreak is attributed to the Bundibugyo variant, a rare Ebola strain for which there is currently no approved vaccine or specific treatment. The World Health Organization has previously declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) and calls for intensified surveillance, contact tracing, early case finding, isolation, and stronger international support to contain spread.

triage.headline_ja: WHOからの警告：致死性ウイルスが制御不能になりつつある
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国イトゥリ州でエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株）の大規模流行が発生し、死者1,556人に達し、WHOがPHEICを宣言しているためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ブンディブギョ株は承認されたワクチン・特異的治療法がなく、WHOがPHEICを宣言済み。死者数・隔離者数が多く、フルRRAが必要。

article.articleHeadline: 新冠又起 山東醫生：急診室擠爆 地上都沒地方躺 | 新冠病毒 | 新冠疫情 | 醫院擠滿人
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: COVID-19 surges again: Shandong doctor says the emergency room is overflowing, there's nowhere to lie on the floor | COVID-19 virus | COVID-19 pandemic | hospitals are crowded
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 surges again in mainland China with fever outbreaks reported in several cities. In Shandong, a doctor and social media posts say emergency departments are overwhelmed; beds are unavailable and some patients lie on the floor. Across Jiangsu, Henan, Shanghai, Hangzhou (Zhejiang), Shanxi, and Beijing, fever cases and SARS-CoV-2 tests have surged, including schoolchildren and households; many infections are linked to a newly circulating variant and more severe symptoms, with longer recoveries. Hospitals warn that patients with milder illness may be turned away as capacity tightens. The Chinese CDC’s latest surveillance (Week 30, July 20–26) shows the proportion of influenza-like illness patients testing positive for SARS-CoV-2 rising to 20.3%, about one in five. Common symptoms include fever, cough, sore throat, and loss of taste, with reports of ongoing community transmission on social media.

triage.headline_ja: 新型コロナ再流行：山東省の医師「救急外来はパンク状態、床に横たわる場所もない」
triage.triage_reason: 中国複数省で新型コロナ様症状の急増と医療機関の逼迫が報告され、新変異株による重症化傾向も示唆されており、IHR基準に複数該当するためフルRRAへの移行を推奨する。
triage.notes: 情報源はNTDTV（大紀元系）であり、中国当局の公式発表とは異なる可能性がある点に留意。中国CDCの週次サーベイランスデータ（ILI陽性率20.3%）は言及されているが、公式発表との整合性確認が必要。新変異株の詳細（名称・重症度データ）は不明であり、続報の確認が望ましい。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola atinge un vârf istoric în RDC: OMS avertizează despre o epidemie "excepțională
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola reaches a historic peak in the DRC: WHO warns of an 'exceptional' outbreak.
article.articleSummary: As of 1 August 2026, Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo reaches a historic peak, with 567 new cases and 296 deaths in the latest week with complete data—the highest weekly toll since the outbreak began. Originating in Ituri, the outbreak has spread to North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo. Healthcare workers comprise 151 infections, 44 deaths. WHO warns that insecurity, large-scale population movements, and cross-border travel hinder response and increase spread risk. No approved vaccine for the Bundibugyo strain; research continues. Hilleman Laboratories (Singapore) is developing what WHO calls the most promising candidate, while Oxford University has started testing an experimental vaccine; the first dose has been given. DR Congo authorities, with WHO and partners, urge a substantial scale-up of interventions to curb this unprecedented epidemic.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱がDRCで史上最高の流行ピークに:WHOは「例外的」な流行と警告
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラ出血熱の週間新規症例・死亡者数が過去最多を記録し、複数州へ拡大、医療従事者の感染も多数でWHOが「例外的」流行と警告しており、IHR基準複数該当・WPRO基準も広く該当する。
triage.notes: Singapore（Hilleman Laboratories）はワクチン開発拠点として言及されているのみで発生地域ではないため除外。感染は複数州（Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, Tshopo）に拡大しているが、いずれもDRC国内のためDRCとして集約。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC : l'épidémie la plus rapide jamais enregistrée dépasse déjà le bilan de 2018-2020
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in DR Congo: the fastest outbreak ever recorded has already surpassed the 2018-2020 toll
article.articleSummary: DR Congo faces the fastest Ebola outbreak on record, declared May 15, 2026 in Mongbwalu health zone, Ituri. By late July 2026, the outbreak reported 3,532 confirmed cases and 1,556 deaths across five provinces, surpassing the 2018–2020 crisis which took over ten months to reach ~2,000 cases and ended near 3,500 cases with ~2,300 deaths. The responsible strain is Bundibugyo, for which there is no approved vaccine or targeted therapy; only early supportive care improves survival. On May 17, 2026, WHO declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. The outbreak has crossed borders, with two confirmed cases in neighboring Uganda, prompting stronger cross-border surveillance, contact tracing, rapid-response teams, and secure treatment centers in hardest-hit areas. Five provinces are now affected.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱がDRコンゴで拡大：史上最速の流行が2018-2020年の被害を既に上回る
triage.triage_reason: PHEIC宣言済みでワクチン未承認のBundibugyo株による過去最速・最大規模の流行がウガンダへ越境しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: ウガンダでの確認例2件が報告されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。WHOは既にPHEICを宣言済み。

article.articleHeadline: രോ​ഗ​പ്ര​തി​രോ​ധ ​സ​ന്ദേ​ശ​വു​മാ​യി ഹെ​പ്പ​റ്റൈ​റ്റി​സ്, ഒ​ആ​ര്‍​എ​സ് ദി​നാ​ച​ര​ണം | Deepika | The Largest Read Malayalam Internet Daily | Online News
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Hepatitis, a disease-prevention message, and OARS Day observance
article.articleSummary: World Hepatitis Day was observed in Kalpetta, Kerala, at the Vellamunda Family Health Center, organized by the Health Department and Health Kerala to raise awareness about hepatitis A, B, and C and preventive measures. Transmission routes highlighted include contaminated drinking water and food, exposure to infected blood, unsafe sexual practices, and reuse of syringes; mother-to-child transmission risk exists for HBV and HCV. The campaign also promotes ORS Day and a Stop Diarrhea campaign to reduce under-five diarrhea deaths, emphasizing oral rehydration solution (ORS), zinc, personal and environmental hygiene, and access to clean water. Inauguration was led by the Panchayat President, with talks by District TB and AIDS Control Officer Dr. Priya Senan, Junior Administrative Medical Officer Dr. Arya Vijaya Kumar on Hepatitis A and ORS, and ART Medical Officer Dr. K.T. Jalib on Hepatitis B and C.

triage.headline_ja: 肝炎、疾病予防メッセージとORSデー観測
triage.triage_reason: 世界肝炎デーに関する啓発活動の報告であり、具体的な感染拡大や異常事態は報告されていない。
triage.notes: 本記事はケララ州における世界肝炎デー及びORSデーの啓発イベントの報告であり、具体的な症例数や発生状況の報告ではないため、対象国リストに該当する感染症イベントとしては扱わない。

article.articleHeadline: Крупнейшая вспышка Эболы
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Largest Ebola Outbreak
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is the largest in history, per the World Health Organization. As of 30 July 2026, there are 3,605 confirmed cases and 1,587 deaths (case fatality rate 44%). In the latest full epidemiological week, 567 cases and 296 deaths were reported, the largest weekly totals to date, signaling exceptionally rapid transmission. The 17th Ebola outbreak began on 15 May in eastern DRC and neighboring Uganda, now affecting three Congolese provinces. The WHO indicates the outbreak is intensifying with ongoing transmission and mounting pressure on health systems. The figures reflect laboratory-confirmed cases, underscoring the urgency of public health response and sustained surveillance across affected regions.

triage.headline_ja: 史上最大のエボラ出血熱流行
triage.triage_reason: WHOが史上最大規模と認定するエボラ出血熱の流行で、致死率44%、感染が複数州・国境を越えて拡大しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: ウガンダへの感染拡大が言及されているが、対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。史上最大規模のエボラ流行として即時フルRRAが推奨される。
